ai_show_review.summary: Primal Dark Star, soaring Eleven jam, tight Alligator‑Caution sequence
ai_show_review.blurb: The set erupts with a monster Dark Star and blistering Saint Stephen before launching into an eleven‑minute Eleven that showcases Garcia’s opening lick and Phil’s shifting bass. Alligator segues into Caution (Do Not Stop On Tracks) and wild feedback to close the show. The Miller soundboard capture is crystal‑clear, making this one of ’68’s most vivid recordings.
ai_show_review.review: On September 2, 1968 at Betty Nelson's Organic Raspberry Farm the Dead delivered a high‑octane, primal performance that still sounds fresh today. Opening with a thunderous Dark Star, Garcia immediately stakes his claim with a searing lick that ripples through an extended jam into Saint Stephen and then into a landmark Eleven—an eleven‑minute odyssey where Phil’s bass weaves in and out of the shifting rhythm while Jerry rides the wave with flawless tone. The band never loses momentum, blasting through The Other One before launching Alligator, which collapses into a ferocious Caution (Do Not Stop On Tracks) → Feedback finale that feels both chaotic and perfectly calibrated. Pigpen’s vocal energy and percussion add an extra spark, and Mickey and Bill lay down a thunderous dual‑drum foundation throughout. The Miller SBD (gd1968-09-02.sbd.miller.115592.flac16) captures the set with outstanding clarity—crisp highs, balanced mids, and no noticeable dropouts—preserving every nuance of this historic ’68 outing.

best_recording.reason: Excellent soundboard capture with crystal‑clear highs, balanced mix and no dropouts; preserves the primal energy of the performance.

key_highlights: Monster Dark Star that sets a volcanic tone
Eleven‑minute The Eleven jam with Garcia’s opening lick and fluid bass work
Alligator → Caution (Do Not Stop On Tracks) → Feedback closing stretch
Blistering Saint Stephen and energetic Pigpen contributions

band_performance.Jerry: Delivers a powerful opening lick on The Eleven and rides the Dark Star and Saint Stephen with flawless, soaring guitar tone.
band_performance.Phil: Provides smooth, shifting bass lines that guide the eleven‑minute jam and lock in tightly with the drums throughout.
band_performance.Bob: Adds crazy rhythm guitar work and strong vocal energy, especially alongside Pigpen’s contributions.
band_performance.Mickey: Drums are thunderous and forward, highlighted by a fierce post‑Alligator solo that drives the set.
band_performance.Billy: Shares the high‑energy dual‑drum assault with Mickey, keeping the momentum relentless from start to finish.
